papers.title: Aperiodic dynamics track cortical state shifts during sleep K-complexes
papers.summary: Using time-resolved spectral parameterization of overnight sleep EEG, the study characterized aperiodic dynamics around expert-annotated K-complexes (KCs) with controls to separate genuine cortical state shifts from waveform artifacts. A component of the KC-locked aperiodic change survived these controls, indicating that KCs are accompanied by a genuine shift toward a higher-exponent, inhibition-dominated cortical state.

papers.title: A systems-level model of sleep-dependent memory-consolidation failure in neurodegeneration: the spindle-slow-oscillation decoupling cascade dissociates amyloid and tau
papers.summary: The authors built a systems-level model coupling cortical slow oscillations, thalamic spindles, and hippocampal ripples to cortical spike-timing-dependent plasticity, and used it to simulate sleep-dependent memory consolidation failure in neurodegeneration. They report that spindle-slow-oscillation timing, not oscillation power, gates consolidation, and that amyloid and tau produce orthogonal signatures (amyloid collapses slow-wave power while sparing replay order; tau the reverse) across the amyloid × tau plane, with a falsifiable prediction that closed-loop slow-oscillation enhancement rescues memory only for coupling/amplitude-dominated deficits.

papers.title: The Asymmetrical Architecture of Ultradian REM Sleep: Direction, NREM Currency, and a Finite Post-REM Predictive Horizon in Mice
papers.summary: The study reanalysed 24-hour recordings from 25 mice to test directionality in ultradian REM sleep organisation, using mixed-effects models, quantile regression, hazard models, and held-out-mouse comparisons. It reports that preceding REM duration predicted subsequent NREM accumulation positively (rho=0.506) across all animals, while accumulated NREM did not predict subsequent REM duration; the REMpre effect became undetectable beyond about 10 minutes of accumulated NREM, supporting an asymmetrical graded refractory regime.

papers.title: EEGDM: Label-Efficient EEG Representation Learning with Generative Diffusion Model.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposed EEGDM, a diffusion-based EEG representation learning framework with a Structured State-Space Model for Diffusion Pretraining (SSMDP) and Latent Fusion Module (LFM). Across TUEV, CHB-MIT, and IIIC benchmarks, EEGDM achieved competitive or superior performance versus state-of-the-art methods, including EEG foundation models, while requiring substantially fewer pretraining and downstream samples.

papers.title: Advancing Translational Phenotyping of Mouse Models for Psychiatric Research by Automated Home-Cage Monitoring.
papers.summary: This review evaluates automated home-cage monitoring (HCM) technologies for translational phenotyping of mouse models in psychiatric research. It argues that continuous, non-invasive HCM captures behavioral dynamics, circadian disruption, social interaction, and stress-related domains with better construct and external validity than short experimenter-driven assays, while highlighting remaining challenges in analytical harmonization, interpretation of high-dimensional data, and alignment with clinically meaningful constructs.

papers.title: Intermittent Cranial Accelerometric Pulses - a Potential Marker of Neurodegenerative Disease
papers.summary: This paper identifies a novel phenomenon called Sleep Bursts (SBs), brief periodic bursts in cranial forces during sleep, characterized in healthy subjects and those with neurodegenerative disease (NDD). SBs occurred at lower rates in NDD subjects, with reduced EEG delta power, suggesting a potential marker for neurodegenerative disease and a possible link to glymphatic drainage.

papers.title: Anesthesia-Informed Approaches to Insomnia: Shared Neural Circuits, Biomimetic Sleep, and Emerging Interventional Strategies.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines convergent neural circuits underlying anesthesia-induced and physiological sleep, appraises evidence for anesthetic agents (dexmedetomidine, ketamine/esketamine, propofol) delivered through non-traditional modalities, and evaluates perioperative sleep optimization for insomnia. It concludes that anesthesia-informed approaches provide mechanistic insights and investigational directions rather than established alternatives to CBT-I or approved hypnotics, highlighting the need for adequately powered insomnia-specific RCTs.

papers.title: Cardiac responses to auditory irregularities reveal hierarchical information processing during sleep
papers.summary: The authors analyzed electrocardiography responses to auditory local-global deviants during wakefulness and sleep in 56 participants to test whether cardiac signals index hierarchical sensory processing. They found cardiac slowing after global deviants specifically during REM sleep, especially tonic REM, and cardiac acceleration effects restricted to light NREM sleep, suggesting cardiac responses can inform state-dependent hierarchical information processing during sleep.

papers.title: Hot take on a cool topic: is there really a need for a systemic master mediator of metabolic suppression in mouse daily torpor?
papers.summary: This perspective argues that daily torpor in mice, induced by caloric restriction and cool environment, does not require a dedicated master mediator for systemic metabolic rate suppression. Instead, centrally mediated changes including cessation of physical activity, reduced thermogenesis, lowered defended minimum body temperature, and reduced cardiovascular work drive the 75-80% drop in metabolic rate, with temperature-dependent effects on biochemical reaction rates accounting for much of the further reduction.

papers.title: Separating personal from population gains when calibrating EEG foundation models for new users
papers.summary: The authors evaluated personal adaptation of three frozen EEG foundation models (CBraMod, REVE, LaBraM) in 235 held-out subjects from three motor-imagery datasets, comparing personal adapters against population models and exchanged adapters. Personal adapters improved mean balanced accuracy by 1.5–5.4 percentage points over the population model and outperformed exchanged adapters by 2.3–7.3 points across all nine model-dataset combinations, but gains shrank with larger population-training budgets and cheap few-label calibration was unreliable, indicating personalization should be evaluated against both population references and exchanged parameters.

papers.title: A Patient-Specific Framework for Separating Temporal Localization from Intracranial Waveform Reconstruction of Interictal Epileptiform Discharges from Scalp EEG
papers.summary: The study developed a patient-specific dual-branch convolutional-attention framework to separate temporal localization from event-specific intracranial waveform reconstruction of interictal epileptiform discharges from scalp EEG in six subjects with simultaneous high-density scalp EEG and intracranial EEG. Results showed that scalp EEG contained recoverable temporal information in some subjects (where accuracy 0.080-0.984, mean 0.333 vs. chance 0.125), but event-specific single-contact morphology was not consistently recovered beyond a fixed patient-specific template (mean waveform correlation 0.752 for model vs. 0.754 for template).

papers.title: The circadian clock regulates KCNH2 (hERG) promoter activity through daily temperature rhythms.
papers.summary: The authors tested whether the human KCNH2 (hERG) promoter is a direct transcriptional target of the circadian clock using luciferase reporter constructs in C2C12 myotubes under serum shock or temperature cycling (36.5–38.5°C). They found a conserved tandem E-box required for promoter oscillation and BMAL1:CLOCK-dependent transactivation, and that dominant-negative CLOCKΔ19 reduced hKCNH2 promoter amplitude under temperature cycling without altering period, concluding that daily temperature rhythms regulate KCNH2 promoter activity through the circadian clock.

papers.title: P-body sequestration of clock transcripts delays repressor synthesis to set circadian period in Drosophila
papers.summary: Using time-resolved proximity labeling, a behavioral RNAi screen, and single-molecule RNA-FISH in Drosophila clock neurons, this study identified P-body components Me31B and Pacman as regulators of circadian period. Sequestration of per and tim transcripts in P-bodies delays translation and repressor synthesis, whereas Pacman-dependent decay terminates repression; Me31B overexpression lengthened the free-running period by approximately 2 hours.

papers.title: Electrophysiological brain reconfiguration during meditation-induced extended cessation of consciousness: an EEG microstate study
papers.summary: Used dense-sampling EEG microstate analysis in five highly trained meditators to characterize brain dynamics during meditation-induced extended cessation (EC) versus counting and memory control tasks. EC was associated with reduced self-related microstate B, increased integrative microstate C, and rerouting of sensory-related microstate A toward integrative rather than self-related processing across multiple frequency bands.

papers.title: Dietary selenium deficiency drives sex-specific circadian disturbance through redox imbalance and causes early systolic dysfunction in mice
papers.summary: Mice fed a selenium-deficient diet for 12 weeks showed reduced plasma selenium, early systolic dysfunction via reduced global longitudinal strain, and cardiac transcriptomic changes enriched for redox, mitochondrial, and circadian pathways. These effects were sex-specific, with a more pronounced cardiac stress response in males.

papers.title: The Gut-Brain Axis in Sleep Deprivation: Mechanisms, Dysbiosis, and Potential Therapeutic Avenues.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized human and animal evidence on how sleep deprivation alters gut microbial communities and immune signaling via the gut-brain axis, converging on circadian/microbial misalignment, inflammatory and barrier dysfunction loops, and altered neurotransmitter and metabolite signaling. It discusses probiotics, prebiotics, postbiotics, synbiotics, diet-based short-chain fatty acid strategies, chronobiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation as biologically plausible but still mainly small-trial or preclinical interventions.

papers.title: Exploring multifaceted mental resilience from the perspectives of sleep and circadian rhythm in healthy adults
papers.summary: In 156 healthy adults assessed with 14-day actigraphy, polysomnography, and dim light melatonin onset, partial least squares regression identified a modest but significant association between greater mental resilience and a sleep/circadian profile marked by greater frontal-central NREM slow-wave activity, greater REM frontal theta, lower occipital spectral power, and probably earlier DLMO. The study was cross-sectional and calls for longitudinal and interventional work.

papers.title: Bright light therapy and circadian rhythm regulation for delirium prevention in hospitalised adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of eight studies (n=1190) evaluated bright light therapy for delirium prevention in hospitalized adults and found an uncertain effect on delirium incidence (RR 0.64, 95% CI 0.38–1.07). Evidence certainty was very low, and circadian outcomes were inconsistently reported.

papers.title: Shenghui Decoction Improves Sleep-Deprivation-Induced Cognitive Impairment in Mice by Modulating Neuroinflammation, NRG1/ErbB4 Signaling, and Purine Metabolism.
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, high-dose Shenghui Decoction improved cognitive impairment and hippocampal histopathology, reduced neuroinflammation, and partially normalized NRG1/ErbB4-related synaptic markers. Integrated network pharmacology and serum metabolomics implicated purine metabolism, with candidate targets APRT, NT5M, ADK, and HPRT1.

papers.title: The association between sleep duration and migraine frequency, disability, and perceived stress in the Headache Assessment via a Digital Platform in United States (HeAD-US) study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 6267 adults with migraine, short sleep (≤6 h) was associated with 10.9% more monthly headache days and 13.6% higher MIDAS scores, while long sleep (≥10 h) was associated with 27.1% more headache days and 66.0% higher MIDAS scores compared with normal sleep. Perceived stress accounted for part of these associations.

papers.title: Decoding obstructive sleep apnea phenotypes through integrated multimodal sleep EEG.
papers.summary: Integrated multimodal sleep EEG with clinical and biomarker data from 309 OSA patients using a cascaded multimodal transformer and consensus clustering, identifying three stable neurophysiological phenotypes. The ten most discriminatory features were all qEEG-derived, and mean AHI did not differ significantly across phenotypes, revealing a dissociation between conventional severity metrics and neurophysiological subtypes.

papers.title: AAV-mediated TBR1 supplementation ameliorates behavioral and electrophysiological abnormalities in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice
papers.summary: Evaluated AAV-mediated human TBR1 supplementation in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice after a single postnatal day 3 retroorbital injection (2E11 vector genomes). Treatment increased TBR1 protein and TBR1/CTIP2/parvalbumin cell counts, improved sociability and food-seeking behaviors, and attenuated elevated relative theta power and social-interaction EEG abnormalities, though anterior commissure abnormalities and some EEG/sleep deficits persisted.

papers.title: Interpreting heart rate variability in clinical context: a framework for understanding a multidimensional autonomic biomarker.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the physiological basis and acquisition methods of heart rate variability (HRV) and proposes a context-aware framework for interpreting HRV as a dynamic signal rather than a standalone diagnostic marker. It emphasizes that HRV interpretation is influenced by measurement modality, duration, circadian timing, behaviors, medications, and comorbidities, and may complement cardiovascular risk assessment when appropriately contextualized.

papers.title: Impact of REM sleep deprivation during the acquisition phase on learning and memory performance, neurotrophic and oxidative stress markers in male rats.
papers.summary: REM sleep deprivation during the acquisition phase in adolescent male rats impaired Morris water maze probe trial memory and increased anxiety-like behavior, accompanied by elevated corticosterone, reduced hippocampal TAS, SOD, and NGF, and increased TOS. The findings link REM sleep disruption with altered memory performance, oxidative balance, and neurotrophic markers.

papers.title: The impact of exam timing on academic performance: Analyzing grades and passing rates in higher education.
papers.summary: Analyzing 400,055 grades from 24,280 Dutch university students across seven academic years, this study found that students perform worse during morning exams and in the week following the start of Daylight Saving Time. The timing effects suggest sleep deprivation contributes to reduced academic performance.

papers.title: Subregion-specific temporal lobe EEG signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: Evidence from high-density EEG.
papers.summary: Resting-state 128-channel high-density EEG in 55 individuals with amnestic mild cognitive impairment and 35 controls revealed increased gamma-band activity across bilateral temporal subregions and elevated delta power and theta/beta ratios mainly in right temporal subregions. Right temporal delta activity was negatively associated with memory performance, and left temporal gamma measures discriminated aMCI comparably to whole-temporal measures.

papers.title: CIRCADIAN CLOCK ASSOCIATED 1 Expression Responds to High Temperature Precisely Through Alternative Splicing in Arabidopsis.
papers.summary: This study shows that Arabidopsis CIRCADIAN CLOCK ASSOCIATED 1 (CCA1) responds to high temperature gradients through alternative splicing, with CCA1βab isoforms upregulated at moderate high temperatures and CCA1 globally upregulated at extreme high temperature. The temperature-dependent shift in CCA1βa-to-CCA1βb isoform ratio fine-tunes biotic stress defense and reactive oxygen species homeostasis, supporting thermal adaptation while preserving circadian stability.

papers.title: Event duration, endotypes and hypoxic burden in obstructive sleep apnoea.
papers.summary: This study examined the association of respiratory event duration with OSA severity and endotypes in 1008 Asian patients with moderate-to-severe OSA. During NREM sleep, longer event durations were associated with higher arousal threshold, greater upper airway collapsibility, lower compensation, longer circulatory delay, and increased hypoxic burden, while AHI alone did not adequately reflect hypoxia-related disease burden.

papers.title: Integrating Behavioral Sleep Medicine with Behavioral Parent Training for Preschool ADHD: Stakeholder Insights for an Early Childhood Intervention.
papers.summary: This qualitative study gathered iterative feedback from parents of preschoolers with elevated ADHD symptoms, pediatricians, and pediatric behavioral health providers on an integrated behavioral parent training and behavioral sleep medicine intervention. Stakeholders emphasized a 24-hour approach, practical developmentally appropriate strategies, caregiver support, and treatment tailoring to family culture and structure.

papers.title: Multimodal predictors of response to intravenous ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: toward personalized treatment in major depressive and bipolar disorders.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided review of 150 studies synthesized multimodal predictors of intravenous ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression, including baseline depressive severity, comorbid anxiety, inflammatory and neuroplastic biomarkers, metabolic factors, genetic variants, neurophysiological signatures, and early symptomatic improvement. It proposes a preliminary clinical framework and pilot questionnaire, while noting that most predictors remain exploratory and require prospective validation.

papers.title: Post-tonsillectomy Respiratory Complications in Children With Obesity: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
papers.journal: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (60,044 children) found that pediatric patients with obesity had significantly higher odds of post-tonsillectomy respiratory complications (OR 1.86, 95% CI 1.38-2.49). The increased odds were observed only when PACU events were included, suggesting discharge may be safe for children with obesity who do not develop complications in PACU.

papers.title: Nocturnal enuresis and maxillary expansion: A narrative review.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Dental Association (1939)
papers.summary: This narrative review critically appraised the evidence linking maxillary expansion to treatment of nocturnal enuresis in children, including three systematic reviews and one randomized placebo-controlled trial using a sham expander. The authors conclude that maxillary expansion is not an evidence-based treatment for nocturnal enuresis and should not be routinely performed in the absence of a transverse discrepancy.

papers.title: Rates and correlates of nightmares and insomnia in active duty military service members pre- and postdeployment.
papers.journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
papers.summary: U.S. Army personnel were assessed pre- and post-deployment to determine rates and correlates of nightmares and insomnia. Nightmares and insomnia, alone and comorbid, were associated with mental health problems, and chronic postdeployment trajectories were linked to higher PTSD, anger, and anxiety symptoms.

papers.title: Immune-neural crosstalk in chronic low back pain: from intervertebral disc degeneration to pain sensitization.
papers.summary: This mini-review examines how immune-neural crosstalk links intervertebral disc degeneration to chronic low back pain through inflammatory mediator release, nociceptor sensitization, and central sensitization. It proposes a systems framework integrating inflammatory biomarkers, endplate imaging, quantitative sensory testing, and neuroimmune imaging to distinguish inflammation-dominant, peripherally sensitized, central-sensitization-associated, nociplastic, and mixed pain profiles.

papers.title: Current knowledge of intermittent photic stimulation for electroencephalography in dogs.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on intermittent photic stimulation for electroencephalography in dogs, noting that protocols vary substantially in stimulus design, vigilance state, and electrode montage. It proposes a framework for standardized awake testing with defined stimulus parameters and improved spatial sampling to enhance diagnostic sensitivity and translational alignment with human epileptology.

papers.title: Prehabilitation for patients undergoing neoadjuvant treatment: results of a single-center pilot study using an integrative medicine day clinic.
papers.summary: This single-arm feasibility trial evaluated an 8-week integrative medicine day-clinic prehabilitation program during neoadjuvant cancer treatment, finding 69% adherence and a within-group improvement in the 1-minute sit-to-stand test, with high patient satisfaction and no adverse events.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of dupilumab in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis with stage 3-5 chronic kidney disease: a retrospective real-world study.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 29 patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis and stage 3-5 chronic kidney disease found that dupilumab treatment for 24 weeks significantly improved skin lesions, pruritus, sleep, quality of life, and frailty, with stable renal function and only mild adverse events.

papers.title: Effects of Rhythm Control versus Rate Control on Atrial Fibrillation and Frailty Development in Older Patients: Protocol for the Cardioversion of Atrial Fibrillation and Frailty in the Elderly (CAFFE) Study, an Observational, Prospective Cohort Study.
Sodium Valproate-Induced Encephalopathy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Case report of a 63-year-old woman on long-term valproic acid who developed encephalopathy with sinus bradycardia despite normal ammonia and therapeutic valproate levels; discontinuation led to rapid and complete resolution.

papers.title: Efficacy of perioperative repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation for postoperative depression in breast cancer patients: study protocol for a single-center randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This is a study protocol for a single-center randomized controlled trial that will enroll 182 breast cancer patients with preoperative depressive symptoms to test whether two perioperative sessions of 10 Hz rTMS over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex reduce the incidence of postoperative depression at day 3 compared with sham stimulation.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
